items.title: CMakeLists.txt only installs AnnotationPanel.py, omitting all helper Python modules and resources

findings.title: CMakeLists.txt only installs AnnotationPanel.py, omitting all helper Python modules and resources
findings.explanation: `AnnotationPanel/CMakeLists.txt` only lists `AnnotationPanel.py` in `KIT_PYTHON_SCRIPTS` and leaves `KIT_PYTHON_RESOURCES` empty. When Slicer builds and packages this extension for the Extensions Manager, CMake will only install `AnnotationPanel.py` into `${Slicer_INSTALL_QTSCRIPTEDMODULES_LIB_DIR}`, omitting all the sibling modules it imports (`AnnotationModel.py`, `ClassLabelTab.py`, `ConfigurationScreen.py`, `ConfigurationValidation.py`, `LabelColors.py`, `PanelWidget.py`, `PresetStorage.py`, `ROITab.py`, `RadiologyTerms.py`, `SegmentationTab.py`, `SliceInfo.py`) as well as the module icon (`Resources/Icons/AnnotationPanel.png`). Consequently, when Slicer attempts to load `AnnotationPanel.py` from an installed extension package, the import check at lines 16-23 of `AnnotationPanel.py` (`import LabelColors`, `import PresetStorage`) will immediately raise `ImportError` and the module will fail to load at Slicer startup.
findings.suggestion: List all Python files required by the module in `KIT_PYTHON_SCRIPTS` (or in a subdirectory package) and add `Resources/Icons/AnnotationPanel.png` to `KIT_PYTHON_RESOURCES` so that `ctkMacroCompilePythonScript` copies and installs them into the extension package.

findings.title: Packaged module omits every required helper script
findings.explanation: The entry point imports LabelColors and PresetStorage immediately and the widget imports PanelWidget and other helpers. None are installed by this CMake target, so a normal packaged installation fails at module import rather than providing the annotation panel.
findings.suggestion: Install all imported Python files alongside the module, and verify the built package in a clean Slicer installation.

claude.reason: AnnotationPanel/CMakeLists.txt lines 6-11 list only AnnotationPanel.py in KIT_PYTHON_SCRIPTS and leave KIT_PYTHON_RESOURCES empty. AnnotationPanel.py lines 16-23 import LabelColors and PresetStorage at import time, and setup() imports PanelWidget. The other helper files in AnnotationPanel/ (AnnotationModel, ClassLabelTab, etc.) are not installed either. A packaged extension therefore raises ImportError on load, and the icon is not installed. Source-tree use works, but the catalog build does not.

gpt.reason: AnnotationPanel/CMakeLists.txt:6-11 lists only `  AnnotationPanel.py` and an empty `set(KIT_PYTHON_RESOURCES`; lines 13-18 pass those lists to the compile/install macro. Root CMakeLists.txt:23-24 only adds this module. AnnotationPanel/AnnotationPanel.py:15-18 immediately does `    import LabelColors  # noqa: F401` and `    import PresetStorage  # noqa: F401`, so an ordinary clean package lacks mandatory imports and cannot load. The icon is also unlisted, although that omission alone does not cause the import failure.

gemini.reason: In AnnotationPanel/CMakeLists.txt:6-11, KIT_PYTHON_SCRIPTS only lists AnnotationPanel.py and KIT_PYTHON_RESOURCES is empty. AnnotationPanel.py:17-18 immediately imports LabelColors and PresetStorage, and AnnotationPanel.py:52 imports PanelWidget (which imports AnnotationModel, RadiologyTerms, SliceInfo, ClassLabelTab, ROITab, SegmentationTab, ConfigurationScreen, ConfigurationValidation). In a packaged extension build, none of those sibling modules are installed, causing module import to fail immediately.

items.title: Importing a different configuration silently overwrites an existing preset

findings.title: Importing a different configuration silently overwrites an existing preset
findings.explanation: When importing a different configuration, the preset name is derived from the imported scan or directory. If that name already exists, save_preset_overwrite truncates and replaces its JSON without asking; importing another package with the same name can destroy the user's previously saved configuration.
findings.suggestion: Check for name collisions and ask before replacement, or save to a unique name; use atomic writes.

claude.reason: PanelWidget.py lines 232-235 call save_preset_overwrite, and PresetStorage.py lines 141-155 overwrite the file with no name-collision check. However, the call is only reached after the user accepts the 'replace the current configuration' dialog (lines 712-716). The overwritten file is a small, re-creatable label preset. This is a usability bug, not a concrete path to harm, so it is not a safety blocker.

gpt.reason: AnnotationPanel/PanelWidget.py:659-666 derives the name and calls the save path: `        preset_name = derive_import_preset_name(record, resolution.directory)` and `        self._apply_imported_label_configuration(record.label_config, preset_name)`. AnnotationPanel/AnnotationModel.py:1337-1354 returns `            return f"Import-{safe}"` using scan or directory data. PanelWidget.py:232-235 calls `            save_preset_overwrite(preset_name, config.to_dict())`; PresetStorage.py:141-146 and 149-154 use `    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:` without a collision prompt. The different-configuration dialog warns of replacing current configuration and annotations, not a separate saved preset. A colliding import name can therefore destroy an existing user preset.

gemini.reason: In AnnotationPanel/PanelWidget.py:232-235 and 663-664, _apply_import_with_new_configuration derives a preset name via derive_import_preset_name(record, resolution.directory) (which produces 'Import-<scan_or_dir_name>', AnnotationModel.py:1337-1356) and calls save_preset_overwrite(preset_name, config.to_dict()). This overwrites any existing preset with the same derived 'Import-<name>' without checking for a collision, though the user already confirmed replacing the configuration in _prompt_import_configuration_choice (PanelWidget.py:615-634) and the name is prefixed with 'Import-'. This is an ordinary UX/soundness issue rather than a blocking safety vulnerability.

items.title: Matching-configuration import clears the current session without confirmation

findings.title: Matching-configuration import clears the current session without confirmation
findings.explanation: The matching-configuration import path calls set_record with its default clear_existing=True, without the replacement prompt used for differing configurations. Existing ROI and segmentation scene nodes and classification annotations are removed, including unsaved work; a subsequent segmentation load can also fail after this destruction.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly confirm replacement whenever existing annotations are present, and load and validate the incoming project before deleting the old session.

claude.reason: When the configuration matches, import_annotations (lines 718-719) calls _apply_import_with_current_configuration, which calls set_record(record) with the default clear_existing=True (lines 548-553). It clears the existing annotations without a prompt. The user explicitly started an import and the label configuration is identical, so replacing the session is expected behavior. At most this is a missing confirmation, which is minor UX and not a safety issue.

gpt.reason: PanelWidget.py:712-718 calls `        self._apply_import_with_current_configuration(record, resolution)` without the differing-configuration prompt; lines 672-675 then call `        self.set_record(record)`. The default in lines 548-553 invokes `            self._roi_tab.clear_and_unbind()` and `            self._segmentation_tab.clear_and_unbind()`. ROITab.py:1544-1549 removes registered scene nodes via `                        slicer.mrmlScene.RemoveNode(node)`; SegmentationTab.py:331-337 removes its segmentation node. PanelWidget.py:579-590 shows the new segmentation load can fail after removal. Unsaved existing work can be lost without an explicit replacement warning.

gemini.reason: In AnnotationPanel/PanelWidget.py:712-719, when label_configs_differ is False, import_annotations calls _apply_import_with_current_configuration (lines 672-678), which calls self.set_record(record) with the default clear_existing=True (lines 548-553) without prompting whether to discard existing in-memory annotations if self._has_any_annotations() is True. Furthermore, if record.segmentation fails to load at line 580, the previous annotations have already been cleared. While real, this occurs when the user explicitly initiates 'Import Annotations' and selects an import file/folder; missing an 'unsaved changes' confirmation dialog on explicit file load is a soundness/UX bug (minor/major), not a blocking safety issue.

items.title: Anatomical slice indices assume voxel axes match anatomical axes

findings.title: Anatomical slice indices assume voxel axes match anatomical axes
findings.explanation: IJK axes depend on the volume's orientation, not on anatomical plane names. For permuted or oblique acquisitions this can export a different voxel axis as the slice index; additionally, index zero falls through to a different calculation in capture_slice_info_for_view.
findings.suggestion: Derive the relevant axis and index from the volume and slice geometry, and explicitly handle zero and oblique views in tests.

claude.reason: SliceInfo.py lines 267-278 map Axial, Coronal and Sagittal to IJK axes 2, 1 and 0. This is only correct for volumes whose voxel axes are aligned with the anatomical axes. In capture_slice_info_for_view, `if anatomical_index:` (line 367) treats index 0 as false and falls back to the offset-based index. This is a real soundness limitation for oblique or permuted volumes, but it only affects exported metadata. I rate it minor.

gpt.reason: SliceInfo.py:267-277 fixes anatomical planes to IJK components, including `        return int(voxel_index_ijk[2])` for axial, without using the volume orientation; permuted or oblique volumes therefore need not have the assumed normal axis. Lines 364-373 use `        if anatomical_index:` so a valid zero instead takes the GetSliceIndexFromOffset fallback. This can give incorrect exported slice metadata; the full IJK and geometric context are also retained (lines 329-362), so the finding does not establish destruction of voxel data.

gemini.reason: In AnnotationPanel/SliceInfo.py:267-278, anatomical_slice_index_from_ijk hardcodes Axial -> voxel_index_ijk[2], Coronal -> voxel_index_ijk[1], and Sagittal -> voxel_index_ijk[0]. Because IJK axes depend on the volume's IJKToRAS orientation matrix rather than fixed anatomical planes, non-LPS/RAS-aligned or sagittal/coronal/oblique acquisitions will pick the wrong voxel axis. Additionally, in SliceInfo.py:364-370, 'if anatomical_index:' treats slice index 0 as falsy and falls through to the offset fallback.

items.title: Slice-view event filters all reference the final loop callback

findings.title: Slice-view event filters all reference the final loop callback
findings.explanation: The eventFilter method closes over the loop-local name _remember_view rather than binding the current callback. After the loop completes, filters can all use the last view's callback, so mouse or wheel events in another view may record the wrong active slice and thus the wrong ROI context.
findings.suggestion: Bind the view name or callback separately to each tracker instance and test interactions in all slice views.

claude.reason: In SliceInfo.py lines 72-80 the eventFilter of the class defined inside the loop calls `_remember_view()`. That name is a free variable of the enclosing function, resolved late, so every tracker calls the last loop iteration's callback. The default-argument binding only protects the callback's own view_name. The bug is real. Its impact is limited because lines 49-70 add per-view slice-modified and interactor observers that bind view_name correctly, so most of the time the active view is still tracked.

gpt.reason: SliceInfo.py:72-79 defines `_remember_view` inside the loop and `                        _remember_view()` inside eventFilter without binding that callback per iteration. Python's shared closure cell therefore points all such filters to the last callback after the loop. ROITab.py:1417-1423 uses `        slice_info = capture_slice_info(self._volume_node)` on ROI finalization, and SliceInfo.py:392-407 obtains the active view from this tracking state. Other slice-node and interactor callbacks at SliceInfo.py:49-70 bind `view_name=name` correctly and can update it too, so actual impact depends on event ordering; incorrect context metadata is plausible, not proven for every interaction.

gemini.reason: In AnnotationPanel/SliceInfo.py:41-84, inside the 'for name in layout_manager.sliceViewNames():' loop, _SliceViewTracker.eventFilter (lines 76-80) calls _remember_view() without arguments, looking up the function name _remember_view in the enclosing install_slice_tracking scope. After the loop finishes, _remember_view is bound to the function created in the last loop iteration (where default argument view_name=name is the final slice view). Consequently, mouse press or wheel events intercepted by the Qt eventFilter on any slice view will record the last loop iteration's view name.

items.title: Export includes patient identifiers without a clear privacy warning

findings.title: Export includes patient identifiers without a clear privacy warning
findings.explanation: Patient ID and DICOM identifiers are automatically captured and written into the user-selected export. Users sharing annotation packages may not realize they contain identifiers: the README mentions series metadata and UIDs but does not explicitly mention patient ID. No automatic network transmission was found.
findings.suggestion: Warn in the export dialog and documentation, and offer a de-identified export option.

items.title: Generic helper module names placed on sys.path at Slicer startup

findings.title: Generic helper module names placed on sys.path at Slicer startup
findings.evidence:
MODULE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
if MODULE_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, MODULE_DIR)

# Fail fast with a clear import error if extension files are incomplete.
try:
    import LabelColors  # noqa: F401
    import PresetStorage  # noqa: F401
findings.explanation: At module import time (which happens during Slicer startup for all scripted loadable modules), `AnnotationPanel.py` inserts its directory at the front of `sys.path` and imports top-level modules with generic names (`LabelColors`, `PresetStorage`, and later `PanelWidget`, `AnnotationModel`, `SliceInfo`, `ROITab`, `SegmentationTab`, `ClassLabelTab`, `ConfigurationScreen`). While Slicer normally adds scripted module directories or packages, placing 11 generic top-level module names in `sys.path[0]` at startup risks name collisions with other Slicer extensions in the shared Python environment.
findings.suggestion: Move the helper modules into a dedicated Python package directory (e.g., `AnnotationPanelLib/`) and install them via `KIT_PYTHON_SCRIPTS`, importing them as `from AnnotationPanelLib import ...`.

findings.title: Entry point alters the process-wide Python import path
findings.explanation: If the directory is not already present, importing the module inserts it at the front of the shared interpreter search path. Generic helper names such as PanelWidget and SliceInfo may then collide with other extensions' imports or already-loaded modules.
findings.suggestion: Package helpers under a uniquely named Python package and use qualified imports without prepending a generic module directory.

items.title: Global slice-tracking observers and event filters are not removed in cleanup()

findings.title: Global slice-tracking observers and event filters are not removed in cleanup()
findings.evidence:
def cleanup(self):
        """Clean up observers when the panel is destroyed."""
        self._remove_scene_observers()
        self._roi_tab.cleanup()
        self._segmentation_tab.cleanup()
findings.explanation: `install_slice_tracking()` in `SliceInfo.py` attaches VTK observers and Qt event filters to Slicer's Red/Green/Yellow slice nodes, interactors, and slice views, storing them in the module-level `_slice_observers` list. Although `SliceInfo.py` defines `remove_slice_tracking()`, `AnnotationPanelRootWidget.cleanup()` never calls `remove_slice_tracking()`, leaving those observers and event filters active after the widget is cleaned up.

items.title: Module category in AnnotationPanel.py ("Annotation") differs from README and catalog ("Quantification")

findings.title: Module category in AnnotationPanel.py ("Annotation") differs from README and catalog ("Quantification")
findings.evidence:
def __init__(self, parent):
        ScriptedLoadableModule.__init__(self, parent)
        self.parent.title = "Annotation Panel"
        self.parent.categories = ["Annotation"]
findings.explanation: The catalog entry and `CMakeLists.txt` specify the category `"Quantification"`, and `README.md` (line 124) instructs users that "The module will appear under the **Quantification** category." However, `AnnotationPanel.py` sets `self.parent.categories = ["Annotation"]`, so users looking under Quantification in Slicer's module selector will not find it there.
findings.suggestion: Align `self.parent.categories` in `AnnotationPanel.py` with the documented category (or update the README).
